key_insight: A two-stage Mamba sequence model can jointly improve superconducting qubit state discrimination and mitigate relaxation errors with better accuracy and far fewer parameters than prior ML readout methods.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets faster, more scalable readout for frequency-multiplexed quantum processors, helping reduce latency and logical error rates in fault-tolerant quantum computing workflows.
method: Stage 1: initial qubit state classification from readout traces
Stage 2: refinement to detect and correct relaxation-induced errors
Uses Mamba sequence modeling for linear-complexity, lightweight inference
evidence_signal: The model reaches a geometric mean readout fidelity of 0.906 (0.911 for the optimal version), cuts parameters by 49.6%, and still achieves 0.893 fidelity at 500 ns readout duration.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on specific trace-length and evaluation settings, so real hardware deployment may require retuning for different devices, noise conditions, or multiplexing layouts.
paper_title: Multi-Stage Mamba-Based Architecture for Fast and Scalable Superconducting Qubit Readout
